process.heading: From first call to final sweep.
process.intro: Five stages, no surprises in between. You'll know who's coming, what's happening and what it costs at every point.

steps.title: The call
steps.body: Tell us what you're thinking. If it's not a job we're right for, we'll say so on the phone rather than waste a visit. Where we can, we'll point you at someone who is.

steps.title: Site visit
steps.body: We come out and look at it properly: ground conditions, access, drainage, what's already there. This is where the real cost of a job reveals itself, and it's why we won't quote blind over email.
steps.timing: Within one working day of your enquiry

steps.title: Planned and priced
steps.body: Drawings and pricing are worked up in-house by the person who'll build it. You get a fixed written quotation with the build-up specified: depths, materials, stages. Not a single number on a compliments slip.

steps.title: On site
steps.body: Work starts on the agreed date with the owner on the tools. Specialist trades are booked in around the programme. Site is swept and made safe every evening, and you get told what's happening tomorrow.

steps.title: Snagged and signed off
steps.body: We walk it with you, write down anything you're not happy with, and fix it before the final invoice. Building control sign-off and any certificates are handed over with the keys.
steps.timing: Final payment only when you're happy

differentiator.heading: Every quote looks the same on handover day.
differentiator.intro: Two driveways can look identical the afternoon they're finished and be three thousand pounds apart. The difference is buried where you'll never see it. It shows up in year three, not week one. Here's exactly what we put underneath.

buildUps.title: Under a driveway
buildUps.note: The corner that gets cut is the sub-base: 75mm instead of 150mm, uncompacted, no membrane. It looks perfect for two summers, then ruts under the car and the joints open up.

buildUps.title: Under an extension
buildUps.note: Footings get dug to the depth the ground actually needs, not the depth that keeps the muck-away bill down. The membrane gets lapped and taped into the wall DPC properly, because damp is unfixable later.

buildUps.title: Under a roof
buildUps.note: A cheap re-roof means tiles over the existing felt and battens. We strip to the rafters, replace anything soft, and you get a roof that's genuinely new rather than resurfaced.

differentiator.closing: Ask every builder you're quoting to write the build-up into the quote. Depth of sub-base, thickness of concrete, whether the roof is being stripped to the rafters. Any decent builder will put it in writing without hesitating. Then the quotes that suddenly look cheap start to make sense.

services.name: Building & extensions
services.cardSummary: Single and two-storey extensions, structural openings and full renovations, footings to shell.
services.imageAlt: A rear extension nearing completion, bifold doors fitted and blockwork ready for render
services.intro: Single and two-storey extensions, structural openings and full renovations, taken from footings through to a shell that's ready to decorate.
services.body:
The person who walks your property is the person who prices it, plans it, and turns up in the morning to build it. Planning is handled in-house rather than farmed out, so the drawings, the quotation and the work on site all come from the same head.

Footings get dug to the depth the ground actually needs, not the depth that keeps the muck-away bill down. The damp-proof membrane gets lapped and taped into the wall DPC properly, because damp is unfixable once the floor is down. Where a specialist is needed (a plasterer for a whole-house skim, an electrician for first fix), we bring in people we've worked alongside for years and rate personally.

A single-storey rear extension is usually eight to twelve weeks from breaking ground to handover. You'll get a realistic programme with your quote rather than an optimistic one designed to win the job.

seo.title: Extensions in Ferndown & Dorset
seo.description: Single and two-storey extensions across Dorset, planned in-house and built by the owner. Fixed written price and a realistic programme.

services.name: Driveways & paving
services.cardSummary: Block paving, porcelain, stone, resin and tarmac on a dug-out, compacted base with proper falls.
services.imageAlt: A finished gravel driveway and rendered retaining wall in front of a bungalow
services.intro: Block paving, porcelain, natural stone, resin and tarmac. All laid on a dug-out, compacted base with proper falls, so it drains away from the house and stays flat.
services.body:
The bit that decides whether a driveway is still flat in year five is the bit you never see. Ours go down on a geotextile membrane with 150mm or more of MOT Type 1, compacted in layers rather than in one pass, then a 30mm sharp sand laying course.

Falls are set so water runs away from the house and into a soakaway or a linear drain, not towards the door. Edge restraints are haunched properly, because a driveway that spreads at the edges has failed no matter how good the blocks were.

The corner that gets cut on a cheap quote is almost always the sub-base: 75mm instead of 150mm, uncompacted, no membrane. It looks perfect for two summers, then ruts under the car and the joints open up.

seo.title: Driveways & Paving in Dorset
seo.description: Block paving, porcelain, stone and resin driveways across Dorset, laid on a properly compacted sub-base with drainage that works.

services.name: Roofing & roofline
services.cardSummary: Full re-roofs, repairs, flat roofs and roofline. Stripped back and rebuilt, not resurfaced.
services.imageAlt: Slate tiles being laid over breathable membrane on a battened roof
services.intro: Full re-roofs, repairs, flat roofs and roofline. Stripped back, checked for rot, re-felted and battened properly. Not tiles laid back over a failing deck.
services.body:
A cheap re-roof means tiles laid back over the existing felt and battens. It buys a few years and hides whatever is rotting underneath. We strip to the rafters, replace anything soft, and lay a breathable membrane across the full area before new graded battens go on.

Tiles can be new or reclaimed depending on what the property needs and what the conservation position is. Leadwork and flashings are formed properly rather than sealed with mastic and hoped for.

Flat roofs are EPDM or GRP, laid on a deck that's been checked rather than assumed. Fascias, soffits and guttering can be done at the same time while the scaffold is already up, which is usually the cheapest time to do them.

seo.title: Roofing in Ferndown & Dorset
seo.description: Full re-roofs, repairs, flat roofs and roofline across Dorset. Stripped to the rafters and rebuilt properly, with a fixed written price.

services.name: Loft conversions
services.cardSummary: Unused roof space turned into a proper room: new floor structure, staircase, insulation and dormers where the headroom needs them.
services.imageAlt: A finished dormer loft conversion clad in grey, above a brick house
services.intro: Unused roof space turned into a room you'd actually want to be in. New floor structure, a proper staircase, insulation, and a dormer where the headroom calls for one.
services.body:
A loft conversion is a structural job before it's a decorating one. The ceiling joists up there were sized to hold plasterboard, not people, so a new floor structure goes in independently of them. Everything else follows from that and from the headroom: where the stairs can land, whether the space needs a dormer, how the roof windows sit in the pitch.

So the first visit is spent in the loft with a tape measure rather than showing you a brochure. If the space works, you'll be told what it can become. If it doesn't, you'll be told that as well, before anyone has spent money finding out.

The person who prices it is the person who builds it, and the quote is a written fixed price with a programme you can plan around.

seo.title: Loft Conversions in Ferndown, Dorset
seo.description: Loft conversions across Dorset. Floor structure, stairs, dormers and roof windows, priced and built by the owner.

services.name: Garage & outbuilding conversions
services.cardSummary: Garages, carports and outbuildings made properly habitable: insulated, floored, lined and finished.
services.imageAlt: A brick outbuilding converted into a room, with new French doors onto the garden
services.intro: Space you already own, made properly habitable. An office, a spare room, a gym, finished to the same standard as the rest of the house.
services.body:
The shell is usually the easy part. What decides whether a converted garage feels like a room or like a garage with carpet in it is what happens to the floor, the walls and the old door opening.

A garage floor is normally laid to fall towards the door so water runs out of it. That has to be levelled and insulated before anything else goes down. The walls are often single skin, so they get lined and insulated rather than simply skimmed. And the up-and-over opening is either built up in matching brick or replaced with doors or a window, depending on what the room is going to be used for.

Done properly it stops reading as a converted garage from the outside as well as the inside.
bullets: Door openings built up or reglazed

seo.title: Garage Conversions in Dorset
seo.description: Garage, carport and outbuilding conversions across Dorset. Insulated, lined and finished by the builder who priced them.

services.name: Kitchen refurbishments
services.cardSummary: Full kitchen refits: strip out, services, floors and units, through to a room that's ready to use.
services.imageAlt: A finished cream gloss kitchen with wood-effect worktops and a built-in double oven
services.intro: Full kitchen refits, from stripping the old one out to a room that's ready to use, including the walls, floors and services hidden behind the units.
services.body:
Most of a kitchen refit is invisible by the time it's finished. The old units come out, and what's behind them is usually where the real work is: walls that were never straight, pipework routed around a layout nobody uses any more, and sockets nowhere near the appliances you've actually bought.

That gets sorted before a single new unit goes back. Floors levelled, services moved to suit the new layout, walls made good. That way the units sit true, the doors line up, and the worktop meets the wall without a bead of filler doing the work.

Whether the kitchen itself comes from a supplier or from you, the room comes back finished rather than handed over to somebody else to tidy up.
bullets: Plumbing and electrics moved to suit

seo.title: Kitchen Refurbishments in Ferndown & Dorset
seo.description: Full kitchen refits across Dorset. Strip out, services, floors and fitting, handled by one team from start to finish.

services.name: Bathroom refurbishments
services.cardSummary: Bathrooms taken back to the walls and rebuilt. Services and waterproofing first, then tiling and fitting.
services.imageAlt: A finished bathroom with marble-effect tiling, a wall-hung vanity unit with a counter-top basin and a round mirror between two windows
services.intro: Bathrooms stripped back to the walls and rebuilt properly. The services and the waterproofing first, then the tiling and the fittings.
services.body:
A bathroom is a small room where everything is either wet or hidden, which is why it's the room most often paid for twice.

Taken back to the walls, the order is what matters: services and falls first, then boarding and waterproofing behind the tiles, then tiling, then fittings. Tile backer board and a proper tanking system in the wet areas cost very little at that stage, and they are the difference between a bathroom that lasts and one that quietly rots behind the grout.

The room comes back finished, including the parts people forget to price, like making good the ceiling and getting the extraction right.

faqs.question: Do you carry out the work yourselves?
faqs.answer: Yes. Every job is planned and priced by the owner, and he's on site working it. Where a specialist trade is needed (a roofer for a full strip, a plasterer for a whole-house skim, an electrician for first fix), we bring in people we've worked alongside for years. You deal with the same person throughout, and he's accountable for all of it.

faqs.question: What areas do you cover?
faqs.answer: Based in Ferndown and covering most of Dorset: Bournemouth, Poole, Wimborne, Christchurch, Verwood, Ringwood, Wareham and the villages in between. Slightly further out, ask anyway; it depends on the size of the job.

faqs.question: Is the quote fixed, or does it move?
faqs.answer: Fixed and in writing. The price only changes if you ask for something extra, or if something genuinely unforeseeable turns up once the ground's open: unrecorded drainage, inadequate existing foundations, rot under a roof deck. If that happens we stop, show you, and agree the cost before continuing. You'll never find out about extra work on the final invoice.

faqs.question: Why is a cheaper quote sometimes a false economy?
faqs.answer: Because the savings almost always come from what gets buried. A 75mm sub-base instead of 150mm. Thinner concrete. No membrane. Tiles laid back over failing battens. On handover day the two jobs look identical. The difference shows up in year three, when the driveway ruts or the ceiling stains. Ask every builder quoting you to write the build-up into the quote.

faqs.question: How long does a typical extension take?
faqs.answer: A single-storey rear extension is usually eight to twelve weeks from breaking ground to handover. Two-storey work runs longer. The variables are ground conditions, how fast building control can inspect, and lead times on anything bespoke like steels or glazing. You'll get a realistic programme with your quote rather than an optimistic one designed to win the job.

faqs.question: Do you handle planning and building regulations?
faqs.answer: The planning side is handled in-house rather than farmed out to a third party. We'll tell you upfront whether your project needs full permission or falls under permitted development, and we'll work to your building control inspector's schedule and be on site for the inspections.

faqs.question: What sub-base do you lay under a driveway?
faqs.answer: For a domestic driveway, typically 150mm or more of MOT Type 1 over a geotextile membrane, compacted in layers rather than in a single pass, then a 30mm sharp sand laying course under the blocks or slabs. Falls are set so water runs away from the house.

seo.title: Privacy Policy
seo.description: How TPS Installations collects, uses and stores your personal data.

privacy.body:
TPS Installations Ltd ("we", "us") runs this website. This page explains what personal information we collect through it, why, and what you can ask us to do with it. We are the data controller for that information.

## What we collect

When you send the quote form we receive your name, phone number, the property postcode, the type of job, the best time to call (if you pick one) and anything you write in the message box. We also note which page of the site you sent it from.

If you phone, text or email us, we keep the details you give us so we can deal with your enquiry.

We do not ask for, and do not want, bank details or anything sensitive through this website.

## Why we use it

We use your details to reply to your enquiry, arrange a site visit, prepare a quote and, if you go ahead, carry out and invoice the work.

The legal basis is that you have asked us to take these steps before entering a contract, and our legitimate interest in answering enquiries about our work. We never sell your details, never add you to a mailing list and never pass them to anyone to market to you.

## Who else handles it

Our website is hosted by Netlify, Inc., which also stores quote form messages and forwards them to our business email. Netlify is based in the United States and transfers data under recognised UK safeguards.

The quote form uses Google reCAPTCHA to stop spam. Google may collect information about your device and how you use the form for that purpose.

If you choose to contact us by WhatsApp, that conversation is also handled by WhatsApp (Meta) under their own privacy terms.

## Cookies and analytics

The site sets no advertising cookies. We use Google Analytics to see which pages are useful, but only if you press Accept on the cookie banner. If you press Reject, or ignore it, Google Analytics is not loaded at all. You can change your mind at any time with the Cookie settings link at the bottom of every page.

Your cookie choice itself is remembered in your browser so we don't ask on every page.

## How long we keep it

If an enquiry does not turn into a job, we delete it within 12 months. If we do work for you, we keep your details and job records for 6 years after the job is finished, because the law requires us to keep business and tax records for that long.

## Your rights

You can ask us for a copy of the information we hold about you, ask us to correct it, ask us to delete it, or object to us using it. Just contact us using the details below. We will reply within one month and there is no charge.

If you are not happy with how we have handled your information, you can complain to the Information Commissioner's Office at ico.org.uk or on 0303 123 1113.

## Changes

If we change how we use personal information, we will update this page and the date at the top.

locationPages.intro:
Ferndown has a lot of bungalows and family homes built in the second half of the last century. They often have good sized gardens, which makes a single-storey rear extension one of the most common requests.

Plenty of these can be done under permitted development, with no full planning application. For a detached house that means up to 4 metres out the back, or up to 8 metres through the prior approval process. For semis and terraces the figures are 3 and 6 metres. We check which applies before you pay for drawings.

Bungalows open another option: building up into the roof. That can add a bedroom and bathroom without losing any garden at all.

Because we are based in Ferndown, we can be on site quickly for the visit, and quickly again if anything needs sorting during the build.
locationPages.localReference: Ferndown is covered by Dorset Council for planning and building control. It is also ringed by protected heathland, such as Ferndown Common.

seo.title: Extensions in Ferndown
seo.description: Single and two-storey extensions in Ferndown, planned in-house and built by the owner. Free site visit and a fixed written price.

locationPages.intro:
A lot of Ferndown homes were built with a single garage and a short drive. Two cars later, the front garden starts to look like the obvious place for more parking.

Before anything goes down, two things need checking. First, paving more than 5 square metres of a front garden with a surface that water can't drain through needs planning permission. Permeable block paving, or a design that runs water onto a planted area, avoids that. Second, if you need a new or wider dropped kerb, that is a separate application to the council.

The part you never see matters most. We dig out to a proper depth, lay a compacted sub-base and edge restraints, then lay the blocks or slabs. Skimping on the base is what makes a new drive sink or spread within a couple of years.

You get a fixed written price after a free site visit.
locationPages.localReference: In Ferndown a new dropped kerb is approved by Dorset Council's highways team, and it has to be in place before you drive over the pavement.

seo.title: Driveways & Paving in Ferndown
seo.description: Block paving, porcelain and resin driveways in Ferndown, laid on a properly compacted sub-base with drainage that works.

locationPages.intro:
Many Ferndown homes are now 40 to 60 years old, which is about the age their original roofs start asking for attention. Slipped or cracked tiles, tired felt, crumbling mortar on ridges and verges, and flat roofs on garages and extensions that have simply worn out.

Not every problem needs a new roof. We look at the whole thing first and tell you straight if a repair will do.

If a full re-roof is the right answer, it is worth knowing the rules. Replacing more than a quarter of a roof is notifiable to building control, and the new roof then has to meet current insulation standards. We build that into the quote rather than finding it out halfway through.

Being local means a leak in Ferndown gets looked at quickly, not added to the end of a long list.
locationPages.localReference: Re-roofing more than a quarter of a roof slope needs building control sign off, which in Ferndown means Dorset Council or an approved inspector.

seo.title: Roofing in Ferndown
seo.description: Re-roofs, repairs, flat roofs and roofline in Ferndown. Stripped to the rafters and rebuilt properly, with a fixed written price.

locationPages.intro:
Bournemouth houses range from big Victorian and Edwardian villas to interwar semis and post-war bungalows. The right extension for each is very different, so we start by looking at how the house is built and how you actually use it.

Rear extensions that open a kitchen onto the garden are the most common request. Side returns can work well on older semis and terraces where there is a narrow strip of unused space.

Plenty of streets here sit in conservation areas. Inside one, some work that would normally be permitted development needs planning permission, and materials usually have to match the house. We check that before any drawings are paid for.

Access is the other thing. On busy roads and tight plots we plan skips, deliveries and scaffold before the first day, so the job doesn't stall.
locationPages.localReference: Planning in Bournemouth goes to BCP Council. Conservation areas include Meyrick Park and Talbot Woods, East Cliff, Boscombe Spa and Southbourne Grove.

seo.title: Extensions in Bournemouth
seo.description: Rear, side and two-storey extensions in Bournemouth, priced and built by the owner. Fixed written quotation, realistic programme.

locationPages.intro:
Parking is tight in a lot of Bournemouth, so turning a front garden into a driveway is one of the most useful jobs we do here.

Two rules apply before a single block is laid. Paving more than 5 square metres of a front garden with a surface water can't drain through needs planning permission, so we usually recommend permeable block paving or a design that drains onto a planted strip. And a new or wider dropped kerb needs separate approval from the council.

In conservation areas the look matters as well. Front boundary walls and the style of paving can be part of what the council wants to keep.

Underneath, it is the same as anywhere. Proper dig out, compacted sub-base, edge restraints, then the surface. That is what stops a drive sinking or spreading, and it is the part a cheap quote cuts.
locationPages.localReference: A dropped kerb in Bournemouth is approved by BCP Council's highways team. You need that approval before you drive across the pavement.

seo.title: Driveways & Paving in Bournemouth
seo.description: Driveways and patios across Bournemouth in block paving, porcelain, stone and resin, on a dug-out and compacted base.

locationPages.intro:
Bournemouth has a lot of older roofs: Victorian and Edwardian slate and clay tile, 1930s concrete tile, and plenty of flat roofs on bays, dormers and rear extensions.

Being close to the sea, roofs here take more wind and weather than they would inland, so fixings, flashings and ridge work need doing properly. That is usually where leaks start.

We look at the whole roof, not just the patch you can see from the garden, and tell you honestly whether it needs a repair or a replacement.

On a full re-roof, replacing more than a quarter of the roof is notifiable to building control and brings current insulation rules into play. In a conservation area, changing the roofing material can also need permission. We check both before we price.
locationPages.localReference: In Bournemouth's conservation areas, swapping a roof covering for a different material can need planning permission from BCP Council, so like for like is often the simpler route.

seo.title: Roofing in Bournemouth
seo.description: Full re-roofs, tile and slate repairs, flat roofs and roofline across Bournemouth. Stripped back and rebuilt, not resurfaced.

locationPages.intro:
Poole covers a lot of ground, from the harbour and Sandbanks through Parkstone and Broadstone to Canford Heath. The homes vary just as much, so no two extensions here are quite the same.

Rear kitchen extensions and garden rooms are common requests. On larger plots, two-storey side and rear extensions come up too.

Some of Poole sits in conservation areas, where more of the work needs planning permission and the design has to suit the street. Near the harbour and coast, some homes also sit in flood zones, which adds a flood risk assessment to a planning application. We check both at the site visit so there are no surprises later.

You get a fixed written price and the owner on site, from the footings through to the finish.
locationPages.localReference: Poole's conservation areas include Sandbanks, Branksome Park and Chine Gardens, Canford Cliffs and Ashley Cross. Planning here is handled by BCP Council.

seo.title: Extensions in Poole
seo.description: Extensions and garage conversions in Poole, planned in-house and worked by the owner. No main-contractor mark-up.

locationPages.intro:
Front driveways are in constant demand across Poole, from Parkstone to Broadstone to Canford Heath, where on-street parking gets harder every year.

Before we dig, we check the rules. Paving more than 5 square metres of a front garden in a surface water can't drain through needs planning permission. Permeable block paving, or directing water onto a planted area, keeps it within permitted development. A new or wider dropped kerb needs its own approval from the council.

Drainage matters more near the coast and harbour, where heavy rain has less room to go. We design the fall and the drainage so water goes where it should, not towards your house or your neighbour's.

Then it is the proper build up: dig out, compacted sub-base, edge restraints and the surface you've chosen.
locationPages.localReference: In Poole, dropped kerb applications go to BCP Council's highways team, and the kerb has to be lowered before a new driveway can be used.

seo.title: Driveways & Paving in Poole
seo.description: Block paved and porcelain driveways and patios in Poole, with soakaways and falls set so water runs away from the house.

locationPages.intro:
Poole's coastal position is hard on roofs. Salt air and strong winds off the harbour and the bay wear fixings, lead and mortar faster than they would further inland.

The most common problems are slipped tiles, failing ridge and verge mortar, worn flashings around chimneys, and flat roofs on extensions and garages that have reached the end of their life.

We start by looking at the whole roof and telling you plainly whether it needs a repair or a replacement.

If it is a full re-roof, replacing more than a quarter of the roof is notifiable to building control, and the new roof must meet current insulation standards. In conservation areas, changing the roof material can also need permission. All of that is checked and priced before we start.
locationPages.localReference: Parts of Poole, such as Sandbanks and Canford Cliffs, are conservation areas where a change of roof material can need planning permission from BCP Council.

seo.title: Roofing in Poole
seo.description: Re-roofs, flat roofs, leadwork and roofline in Poole. Stripped to the rafters, rotten timber replaced, membrane across the full area.

locationPages.intro:
Wimborne mixes a historic town centre with Victorian terraces, interwar houses and newer estates towards Colehill and Merley. Each needs a different approach to an extension.

In the centre, the conservation area means more of the work needs planning permission, and materials need to suit the building. On newer homes, a single-storey rear extension can often go ahead under permitted development.

The rivers matter here too. The Stour and the Allen meet at Wimborne, and homes close to either can sit in a flood zone. That adds a flood risk assessment to a planning application and can affect floor levels. We check it at the first visit.

Wimborne is ten minutes from our base in Ferndown, so we are close by for the whole build.
locationPages.localReference: Wimborne sits in Dorset Council's area. Its town centre is a conservation area, and land near the Stour and the Allen can fall in a flood zone.

seo.title: Extensions in Wimborne
seo.description: Extensions and renovations in Wimborne from a builder ten minutes away in Ferndown. Fixed written price, owner on the tools.

locationPages.intro:
Around Wimborne, a lot of homes on older streets were never built with off-road parking in mind, so turning a front garden into a driveway is a common request.

The rules are the same across England. Paving more than 5 square metres of a front garden in a surface water can't drain through needs planning permission, so permeable paving or a planted soakaway strip is usually the way to go. A new or wider dropped kerb needs separate approval from the council.

Drainage deserves extra thought here, with the Stour and the Allen close by. We design falls and drainage so rainwater soaks away properly rather than running onto the road or towards the house.

Underneath, it is dig out, compacted sub-base, edge restraints, then the finish. That is what keeps a drive level for years.
locationPages.localReference: In Wimborne, dropped kerbs are approved by Dorset Council's highways team. Inside the town centre conservation area, front boundary changes can also need consent.

seo.title: Driveways & Paving in Wimborne
seo.description: Driveways, patios and retaining walls in Wimborne, laid on 150mm or more of compacted MOT Type 1 over a geotextile membrane.

locationPages.intro:
Wimborne has some of the oldest buildings in the area, from the historic centre to Victorian terraces and cottages, alongside newer homes on the edge of town.

Older roofs need a careful eye. Original slate and clay tiles can often be reused, and matching materials matters, especially in the conservation area where a change of roof covering can need planning permission.

On newer homes the usual issues are slipped tiles, tired ridge mortar and flat roofs on extensions and garages that have worn out.

We look at the whole roof first and tell you honestly whether it needs a repair or a replacement. If more than a quarter of the roof is being replaced, that is notifiable to building control and brings current insulation rules in. We price all of that up front.
locationPages.localReference: Wimborne's town centre is a conservation area under Dorset Council, so like for like materials are usually the simplest route when a roof is replaced there.

seo.title: Roofing in Wimborne
seo.description: Full re-roofs, repairs and roofline in Wimborne. New battens, breathable membrane and any soft timber replaced before tiles go back.
